summary: Gone Forest Service lookout in Clackamas County: 1931 tent, 1939 20-foot L-4 tower, deactivated 1964; a 2020 hike found footings, not a tower.

facts.status_note: Removed in the 1960s; a 2020 hiking account found concrete footings and no tower.

access.note: By 2020 a berm on the forest road stopped vehicles where the hike began. No current access rule was found in any source.

visit.trail_note: About 2.2 miles on foot along the old road from the berm to the spur road up to the summit (2020 hiking account).

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com both give the tower as 20 feet (6.1 m). The 4.6 m figure (about 15 feet) matches the lookout house height in the 1947 survey, a different measurement.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1932 newspaper item says a new lookout station was completed at Bedford Point that July. The register and firelookout.com date the 20-foot L-4 tower to 1939. No source says whether the 1932 station and the 1939 tower are the same structure.
The register says gone by 1969, the history page says deactivated in 1964 and removed, and the 2020 account says removed in the 1960s. Read together, they give a removal between 1964 and 1969.

notes_for_editor: Four sources, all hobbyist or database compilations; no Forest Service record was found. The 1932 station and 1939 tower conflict is unresolved. The 2020 account is the only description of the site today and is a personal hike. Firelookout.com credits photos to the USFS and Jim Doerter, but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed. The brief's agency and elevation match the sources.
